title: Move a fingerprinted glass into an evidence box, touching only its inside
instruction: The glass is evidence with fingerprints on its outside, so touch it only on the inside: put a gripper's fingers into it nearly closed, then open them against its inner walls. With the left gripper move it from its yellow mark onto the white exam sheet, then with the right gripper into the brown evidence box, standing on the box floor, and let go. Never let its outside touch anything, and set it down only on its mark, the sheet or the box floor.
context: Crime-scene investigators and evidence technicians (O*NET 19-4092.00 Forensic Science Technicians, 33-3021.00 Detectives and Criminal Investigators) must not smear or add latent prints: a drinking glass with prints on its outside is lifted with gloved fingers spread inside it, never gripped round its sides, set on a clean examination sheet to be documented, and moved on so that nothing touches its outside. The task covers that handling for latent prints only: the box is the transport box it is set into; fixing it there (a dowel or ties) and swabbing the lip for DNA, which fingers inside would touch, are later steps, out of scope. As a robot task it is contact discipline on one object for a whole trial, with an unusual expanding internal grasp and rules on where it may touch down. Gripping from above, only the left arm reaches the glass's start, only the right the box; the exam sheet on the midline is the one place both reach.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Four things are on the table. (1) Glass: a loose square drinking glass (a rocks glass) of pale blue tinted clear acrylic, open at the top, outside 74 x 74 mm and 80 mm tall, with 6 mm walls and a 6 mm floor (the opening is 62 x 62 mm, 74 mm deep inside), 0.18 kg, standing upright on the start mark, centred at x 26.0 cm, y +38.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. Its outside stands for a surface holding latent fingerprints. (2) Start mark: a yellow card, 110 x 110 mm and 1 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 26.0 cm, y +38.0 cm (the glass has 18 mm of card on every side). (3) Exam sheet: a white paper card, 140 x 140 mm and 2 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 27.0 cm, y 0 (on the midline). (4) Evidence box: an open box of brown cardboard with four walls 5 mm thick and 55 mm tall round a 105 x 105 mm floor (outside 115 x 115 mm), fixed to the table, centred at x 26.0 cm, y -38.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y; in simulation the table top is its floor (a real build uses a box with a thin floor, taped down). Gripping from above, only the left arm reaches the glass's start and only the right arm the evidence box; both reach the exam sheet. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the glass and each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (between the tips) and opening (0 closed, 1 open: pads 94 mm apart). Each finger is a block 10 mm thick outside the pad gap and 40 mm wide (its size 19-38 mm above the tips), along the gripper's axis as tilted; the scorer cannot see the gripper's turn about that axis, so it tries every turn 0-175 degrees in 5-degree steps. Finger rule, in the glass's frame: a gripper is fine if no part of its fingers' lowest 38 mm can reach below the rim; or if, at every turn, all of it is at least 10 mm from the glass (outside a box 10 mm bigger on every side and under its bottom); or if both fingers, wherever below the rim (for a tilted gripper also as far above it as they could swing), lie in the opening within 5 mm of the inner walls and above the inner floor, each counted up to its carriage 70 mm above the tips: at some turn if the tip point is in the glass, else at every turn. Score 0 if at any moment: (1) a gripper breaks the finger rule (a finger on the glass's outside or within 1 cm of it); (2) the glass comes within 2 mm of a box wall, seen from above, while its lowest point is less than 2 mm above the wall's top; (3) it tilts more than 10 degrees; (4) its lowest point is less than 4 mm above the table top while its outline seen from above is not wholly on the start mark, the sheet or the box floor; (5) it moves down faster than 0.45 m/s (a 1 cm fall) without a finger-tip point inside it moving down with it (within 0.15 m/s); (6) it leaves the table (lowest point 10 mm below the top, or centre beyond its edge); (7) the grippers cannot be read on more than 1% of the steps (on such a step rules 1 and 5 are skipped and 'let go' is taken as met). 'Standing on' a surface: tilted under 5 degrees, outline wholly on it, lowest point within 3 mm of its top, still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). 'Let go': the finger-tip point 20 mm above the rim or 60 mm from the glass's axis. Otherwise: 1.0 if the glass stands in the box (on its 105 x 105 mm floor) with both grippers let go, having stood on the exam sheet earlier; 0.75 if it stands in the box but a gripper has not let go or it never stood on the sheet; 0.5 if it stands on the exam sheet; 0.25 if it was lifted at some moment (lowest point 20 mm above the table) but none of the above holds; 0 otherwise. The score is read at the last step; the trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s. Real trial: dust the glass's outside with fingerprint powder or chalk; film from two sides at right angles and from above, with a 2 cm scale bar on the box; judge rule 1 frame by frame (below the rim each finger inside the glass or at least 1 cm from it; the powder shows any touch), rules 2 to 6 from the same videos, the end state with a ruler.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The glass is one rigid acrylic box held by friction on its inner walls; the evidence box is four fixed walls with the table as its floor. Latent prints are not simulated: touching is judged from the glass's pose and each gripper's fingers (as blocks at any turn about its axis), not from the gripper's body or the arm above them.
reset_notes: Stand the glass upright back on its yellow start mark, centred at x 26.0 cm, y +38.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. The start mark, exam sheet and box are fixed. Nothing is consumed; in a real build wipe the glass and dust its outside again with fingerprint powder or chalk before each trial, so that any touch on the outside shows.
